what_happened.line: The newly elected Sewer Commission chose its officers: a chairman, a vice chair and a clerk, each by a vote that passed.
A commitment for final water reads at sales was approved.
A motion to waive grease trap annual permit fees for FY21 was made, but the minutes record the vote result as not audible.
The commission said an irrigation policy change will go on a future agenda, and a letter will give residents another 30 days to pay meter fees.
Woodard & Curran and Fitchburg invoices were approved for payment.

why_it_matters: Irrigation meter fees, which about half of those billed had paid, may get a nonpayment rule, so households with irrigation meters could face a new penalty process.
Sewer costs reach residents as fees and as payments to Fitchburg, and the grease trap waiver, if adopted, would remove a permit fee for food service businesses for a year.
watch_next: A future agenda item on the irrigation policy change, and the letter giving residents another 30 days to pay.
The recorded result of the grease trap fee waiver vote, and the closing on the LNT trust property that owners planned for July.
